No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not prove complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown, with open banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not proof of exploitation. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates; permit only bounded reversible growth that preserves existing consent, disclosures, data handling, claims, and access boundaries. Do not create or requeue production work, change credentials or permissions, add dependencies, deploy, access private containers, exploit targets, or conduct external outreach. Continue the existing read-only security evidence matrix; do not claim certification or a clean bill of health.

Retain the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Record dated, redacted evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness.
